title: Over-Cap Claim Value (Cartwise Grocery Orders Glossary)
content:
**Over-cap claim value** (Cartwise Grocery Orders). For the over-cap amount of a line billed although the shopper recorded its product as not found, the claim value of that line depends on how its billed unit price compares with the original unit price on the line:

- when the billed unit price is **below** the original unit price, the claim value is the original unit price times the billed units, rounded to the cent;
- when the billed unit price is **above** the original unit price, it is the average of the two prices times the billed units, rounded to the cent;
- when the two prices are **equal**, the line is not re-priced and the claim value is the line's billed charge.

Both prices and the billed units are read from the not-found line's billed line entry: the original unit price is the price of the product originally ordered, the billed unit price is the price actually billed, and the billed units are the quantity billed. Rounding is to the cent, half up, and happens once, on the product of price and units; the average of the two prices is not rounded on its own.

### Comparison table

| Billed unit price against original | Claim value |
|---|---|
| Lower | Original unit price times billed units, rounded to the cent |
| Higher | Average of the two prices times billed units, rounded to the cent |
| Equal | The line's billed charge |

### Boundary illustrations (hypothetical figures, 3 billed units, original unit price 4.00)

| Billed unit price | Billed charge | Claim value |
|---|---|---|
| 3.50 | 10.50 | 4.00 times 3, that is 12.00 |
| 3.99 | 11.97 | 4.00 times 3, that is 12.00 |
| 4.00 | 12.00 | 12.00 (billed charge) |
| 4.01 | 12.03 | average 4.005 times 3, that is 12.015, rounded to 12.02 |
| 4.60 | 13.80 | average 4.30 times 3, that is 12.90 |
